full_judgment: 4. The Rule was opposed by the respondent No.5 by filing affidavit-in-opposition stating, inter alia, that the writ petition so filed is not maintainable being barred by limitation, estoppel, waiver and acquiescence since the writ-petitioner challenged the amended schedule which was made on January 23, 1986 and as under the said Rule the writ-petitioner was appointed in Grade-ll because of his qualification and he joined in Grade-11 on January 18, 1995 while the respondent No.5 joined in Grade-I on December 26, 1994, that had the writ-petitioner been aggrieved because of his appointment in Grade-II he ought to have challenged the legality of the amended Rule immediately after he noticed his appointment in Grade-II and having had not done so the petitioner being guilty of latches in filing the writ petition only in 2001 same was bad for latches and delay, that the writ petition for all practical purposes being related to the claim for grade and promotion the same is not maintainable and that the matter of promotion is exclusively matter for adjudication by the Administrative Tribunal, that in the advertisement made by the Bangladesh Public Service Commission in 1994 for filling up two posts of Engineer and Ship Surveyor therein qualification and experience with the pay scale against the respective grade were specifically mentioned, that writ-petitioner having and had accepted his appointment in Grade-II and having had joined in the said grade subsequent to the date of joining of the respondent No.5 the writ-petitioner's contention that the respondent No.5 is junior to him is not tenable, that the writ petition has been filed for the speculative purpose of creating a dispute and to delay the promotion cif the respondent No.5 who is fully eligible for promotion on a regular basis, that writ petitioner having had filed an application for promotion to the Grade-I upon completion of 5 years-service in Grade-11 same clearly shows that the writ petition was filed for malafide purpose of delaying the promotion due to the respondent No.5 and the writ-petitioner cannot make any claim as he is not in the feeder post or in the range of promotion, that for the redress of his grievance against giving current charge to the respondent No.5 the writ-petitioner was required to move the Administrative Tribunal and that the redress so sought as regard the giving of current charge to the respondent No.5 is not available in the writ jurisdiction.
